title: Biorthogonal Time-Dependent Variational Principle for Non-Hermitian Systems
abstract: We develop a biorthogonal time-dependent variational principle for real-time dynamics of non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems. Independent left and right matrix-product states obey coupled bivariational tangent-space equations whose cross-Gram matrix defines an oblique projection. A matrix-free scaled Taylor action propagates the resulting non-normal local generators without assembling dense matrices or storing a Krylov basis. We distinguish the fully coupled algorithm, which solves the cross-pairing problem and truncates the two bond bases jointly, from an efficient independently propagated approximation used for large systems. Independent truncation can make the retained left-right pairing nearly singular; overlap drift and the smallest singular value of the bond cross matrix expose this failure, while coupled truncation substantially delays it. Exact benchmarks and convergence tests validate the method. Applied to an interacting long-range non-Hermitian Ising chain, it resolves a biorthogonal dynamical quantum phase transition and shows that a weak imaginary field shifts the leading critical time from $t^{\ast}|J|=1.84$ to $1.04$.
summary: This paper introduces a biorthogonal Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) designed to simulate non-Hermitian quantum dynamics accurately. It rigorously compares fully coupled versus independently truncated algorithms, demonstrating that the coupled approach is necessary for maintaining numerical stability near critical points. The method successfully applies to study dynamical quantum phase transitions in models exhibiting gain and loss.
main_problem: Developing a robust and efficient time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) for simulating the real-time dynamics of non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The fully coupled biorthogonal TDVP successfully resolves a dynamical quantum phase transition (DQPT) and maintains numerical stability significantly longer than independent approximation schemes.
method: The authors employ a biorthogonal TDVP framework, utilizing a matrix-free scaled Taylor action to propagate coupled left and right matrix-product states (MPS) in a manner that respects the non-Hermitian structure.
model_or_system: The method is applied to various non-Hermitian models, including the interacting long-range non-Hermitian Ising chain and the disordered Hatano-Nelson chain, which model open-system dynamics or gain/loss processes.
key_observables: Biorthogonal expectation values, overlap drift ($\epsilon_{ov}(t)$), and the gauge-invariant biorthogonal return rate ($\lambda_{bi}(t)$).
important_parameters: The critical time scale $t^*/|J|$, and the coupling strength $k$ in the Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of the TDVP ansatz, and the comparison highlights the failure modes when independent truncation is used versus the coupled approach.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of coupled vs. independent truncation schemes regarding overlap drift and show the successful tracking of a DQPT cusp using the coupled method.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the biorthogonal TDVP, details the fully coupled vs. independent algorithmic implementations, validates the method against exact diagonalization (ED) benchmarks, and applies it to study DQPTs in specific non-Hermitian chains.
why_interesting: This work provides a state-of-the-art numerical tool for simulating non-Hermitian dynamics, which is crucial for modeling open quantum systems where gain/loss or measurement backaction are dominant effects.
